parts.text: A student investigates the balancing of a metre ruler. Fig. 1.1 shows the apparatus. Fig. 1.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) The student places a metre ruler on a pivot at the 50.0 cm mark. She places an object Q with its centre on the metre ruler at the 90.0 cm mark. Determine the distance y from the 50.0 cm mark to the centre of the object Q. y = ................................................... cm [2]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) She places a 2.0 N load on the metre ruler. She adjusts the position of the load so that the metre ruler is as near as possible to being balanced. She measures the distance x from the centre of the load to the 50.0 cm mark. 21.5 x = ......................................................... cm

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Calculate the weight W of object Q, using the equation W = x y × 2.0 N. Give your answer to a suitable number of significant figures for this experiment. W = ..................................................... N [2] She repeats the procedure, using a 3.0 N load. She does not change the position of object Q. 14.8 x = ......................................................... cm

ms.label: 1(b)(i)
ms.text:
W = 1.075 / 1.08 / 1.1
W given to 2 or 3 significant figures

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate a new value of the weight W of object Q, using the equation W = x y × 3.0 N. Give your answer to a suitable number of significant figures for this experiment. W = ...................................................... N [1]

ms.label: 1(b)(ii)
ms.text: New W given to same number of significant figures as in (i)

ms.label: 1(c)
ms.text:
Statement to match results
Explanation with (W values quoted and) matching statement and results

ms.label: 1(d)
ms.text:
A diagram clearly showing a suitable approach e.g. edges of object Q symmetrically either side of 90.0 cm mark.
Or wording describing the method.

ms.label: 1(e)
ms.text:
Repeat and average OR Move the load back and forth / slowly (to establish the range within which the balance point resides
or until best balance).

parts.label: f
parts.text: (f) Fig. 1.2 Fig. 1.2 shows the metre ruler balanced on the pivot with no loads. The balance point shows the position of the centre of mass of the metre ruler. Determine the distance d between the 50.0 cm mark on the metre ruler and the centre of mass. Show your working. d = ......................................................... [2]

ms.label: 1(f)
ms.text:
3 mm OR 0.3 cm
Correct working shown
